title: Ulugh Beg
summary: Ulugh Beg, born in 1394 in Soltaniyeh, ruled Transoxiana from 1409, founded a school at Samarkand in 1420 and built an observatory there. His Zij-i Sultani star catalogue, published in 1437 per MacTutor, gives positions of 992 stars. He was executed at Samarkand in 1449 on his son's orders.

uncertainty.note: Exact birth and death dates are given by MacTutor.

where.modern_name: Ulugh Beg Observatory site, Samarkand, Uzbekistan (pinned to his observatory; he was born at Soltaniyeh, Iran)

importance.justification: MacTutor calls his catalogue the first comprehensive stellar catalogue since Ptolemy and says it set the standard until the seventeenth century.

reviewer_note: Sources disagree: MacTutor says observatory construction began in 1428 and the catalogue lists 992 stars (1437); the IAU-UNESCO page says the observatory was founded four years after the 1420 school and dates the Zij to 1438-39. Summary omits the observatory start date for that reason. His madrasa fronts the Registan; MacTutor says his tomb was found in 1941 in a mausoleum Timur built in Samarkand (Gur-e-Amir link rests on that description, not verified).
